We're backed by leading venture and edtech investors including Bessemer Venture Partners (Shopify, LinkedIn, Anthropic, Perplexity) and Owl Ventures (Newsela, Quizlet, MasterClass), with a team spanning top AI companies and real classroom experience. We're a fast-moving, collaborative team driven by a shared commitment to educator impact and product excellence. Our values—urgency, ownership, and focus—shape how we build and who we are. THE OPPORTUNITY: We're looking for a Senior Field & Experiential Marketing Manager who gets genuinely excited about the full arc — from a wild idea on a whiteboard to the moment a teacher posts a picture of your activation on Instagram and tags all their friends. This is not a "manage the booth vendor and ship the banners" role. This is a creative and strategic builder role — one that's as much about inventing new ways to show up for teachers as it is about executing the playbook we've already started. Conference and trade show presence is part of it. But the bigger opportunity is everything beyond that: surprise-and-delight activations in teacher communities and own Brisk events, pop-ups, grassroots moments, and formats the edtech world hasn't seen yet. You'll be as comfortable hauling equipment and problem-solving on-site as you are pitching a bold new concept to leadership or pulling post-event attribution data. You think in experiences, not checkboxes. Conferences are just the beginning. WHAT WE'VE BUILT: We're not starting from zero. Here's a taste of what Brisk has already pulled off — and why we need someone to take it to the next level. The Brisk-It Barbeque — Our flagship conference booth isn't a booth. It's a backyard. Fake grass, hay bale seating, picnic tables, string lights, marquee letter signage, a brick backdrop, and a photo wall built for sharing. At our last major conference, we ran a full programming schedule out of the space — named sessions, educator creator takeovers, live feature drops, and a Slam Poetry Night. Teachers didn't just stop by. They came back. Swag teachers actually keep — We think hard about what ends up in a teacher's bag versus a hotel trash can. The result is merch people seek out at our booth, show off on social, and carry into their classrooms. We're looking for someone who raises the bar on this every single time. The bar is already high. Your job is to raise it. YOU WILL: End-to-End Execution Own logistics from concept to load-out: venue/vendor sourcing, budget management, permitting, staffing, swag, setup, and teardown. Be the person on the ground making it work — and make it look effortless. Build repeatable playbooks so great activations can scale. Experiential Strategy & Creative Ideation Take ownership of Brisk's field and events strategy and make it better — conference presence, owned events, community activations, and formats we haven't tried yet. Dream up and pitch bold, memorable concepts that make teachers stop, engage, and share — then figure out how to actually execute them. Evolve our signature moments (yes, including the BBQ booth) into an expanding portfolio of experiences that people genuinely talk about. Growth & Attribution Define success clearly before every event: teacher signups, MAU lift, pipeline influenced, social impressions, share-worthiness. Work with the broader marketing team to connect field activity to measurable teacher growth and district pipeline. Report on ROI with rigor and push for continuous improvement. Cross-Functional Partnership Collaborate with brand, paid, lifecycle, and community teams to amplify event impact before, during, and after. Partner with the sales and district team to align field presence with ABM and pipeline goals. Brief the creative team and outside vendors with clear direction. YOU HAVE: 5+ Years of Experience : Field marketing, events, partnerships, or related roles in a high-growth venture-backed startup. Built memorable in-person experiences — booths, activations, or events that people photographed, shared, and talked about for months. Experience being deeply comfortable in the details and the big picture — you can sketch the concept and pull the permit. Energy and confidence on-site; things go sideways and you handle it. Thoughts about the after — what did we capture, who signed up, what did we learn? Natural collaboration skills - you can sell an idea internally and execute it externally. The American hardwood industry has lost more than half its sawmills in the last two decades. Quality trees go to waste, and the US imports more lumber than it produces, even though domestic capacity could meet nearly all of our needs. Until now, this industry forced a choice: local relationships or national scale, meaningful materials or modern efficiency. We don't think those are real tradeoffs. We're building the infrastructure to prove it, with modern software, better supply chains, and a clear view of what comes next: a wood economy that's local, efficient, and built to last. You’ll oversee a national supplier, production, and distribution network that includes both vertically integrated hubs and a rapidly expanding ecosystem of third-party partners. You’ll bridge the gap between high-level strategy and on-the-ground execution, creating the critical infrastructure needed to enable historic volume growth. This is a role for a battle-tested operator who embodies Extreme Ownership and thrives at the intersection of people and process management. You embody Cambium’s “extreme ownership” and “people first” core values in your management approach. Operational & Financial Rigor: you have a proven ability to design and optimize manufacturing and distribution systems, leveraging data to drive performance improvements. You’re capable of implementing real-time dashboards to drive accountability across production teams – specific experience with NetSuite preferred. Quality at Scale: You’re well versed in establishing QA/QC protocols (e.g., Six Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, or ISO standards) that significantly reduced failure rates, waste, and "re-work" costs. The Intelligence and Investigations team supports this by identifying and investigating misuses of our products – especially new types of abuse. This enables our partner teams to develop data-backed product policies and build scaled safety mitigations. Precisely understanding abuse allows us to safely enable users to build useful things with our products. About the Role As an Abuse Investigator on the Intelligence and Investigations team, you will be responsible for detecting misuse of our platform or services. Specifically, you will focus on cases where users attempt to use our platform in connection with prohibited activities such as developing or delivering biological and/or chemical threats to harm people, critical resources/infrastructure, or the environment. OpenAI has strict prohibitions and policies in this area, and you will detect, disrupt, and enforce on actors who violate our policies. This role requires domain-specific expertise, experience investigating sophisticated threats, and the ability to navigate ambiguous signals in a complex and adversarial threat environment. You will respond to time-sensitive escalations and will be expected to present your investigative work, both in writing and verbally, to key stakeholders across government, industry, and civil society, when required. You will also help inform the company’s evolving threat response and integrity monitoring and mitigation stack, while working closely on individual cases and enforcement assessments. This role is remote-friendly, though you’re welcome to work from our San Francisco office if desired. Some investigations may involve sensitive content of a violent or graphic nature. Communicate findings from your investigations with internal stakeholders and leadership and, at times, external partners including regulatory or scientific organizations. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. At the heart of Defining Possible is our commitment to missions. In rapidly changing global security environments, Northrop Grumman brings informed insights and software-secure technology to enable strategic planning. We’re looking for innovators who can help us keep building on our wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies that fuel those missions. At Northrop Grumman, you’ll have the resources, support, and team to do some of the best work of your career. We are looking for you to join our team as a Principal/Senior Principal Board Designer based out of Baltimore, MD. This role may be staffed as Hybrid out of Baltimore/Linthicum, MD. The Principal/Senior Principal Board Designer is a core member of the eCAD team responsible for creating high quality printed circuit board (PCB) layouts that meet the electrical, mechanical, and manufacturability requirements of our products. You will work closely with schematic designers, hardware engineers, mechanical designers, and the manufacturing team to translate concepts into production ready board designs, supporting a broad portfolio of defense grade products. What You’ll Get to Do Develop complete PCB layouts – From component placement to routing, create multi-layer board designs that meet signal integrity, power distribution, and EMC requirements. Perform design rule checks (DRC) and sign off – Run automated DRC, signal integrity simulations, and thermal analyses; resolve violations and document compliance. Collaborate on cross functional design reviews – Present designs to electrical, mechanical, and reliability teams; incorporate feedback and drive design closure. Generate production documentation – Produce TGZ, drill files; ensure data integrity in the PLM system.  Mentor junior designers – Provide guidance on best practices, standards, and tool usage; lead short technical workshops within the eCAD group. Stay current with industry trends – Evaluate emerging PCB technologies (high speed, flex rigid, HDI) and recommend tooling or workflow improvements. This role may be filled as a Principal Board Designer or a Senior Principal Board Designer. This position is contingent on the ability to obtain/maintain an active U.S Government Secret clearance or the successful transfer of one, prior to start. Minimum of 5 years of hands on PCB layout experience in a high volume or high complexity environment (digital, mixed signal, or RF). Minimum of 3 years of experience with Mentor Graphics (including advanced routing and stack up configuration).  Alternate routing software experience will be considered. Minimum of 3 years of working knowledge of IPC 2221, IPC 6012 & 13, IPC 7351, and GD&T for PCB design. Basic Qualifications for Senior Principal Board Designer Bachelor’s Degree with 8 years of experience, master’s degree with 6 years of experience, Ph.D. with 4 years of experience in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics or related technical fields; an additional 4 years of experience may be considered in lieu of a degree U.S Citizenship is required. Minimum of 5 years of hands on PCB layout experience in a high volume or high complexity environment (digital, mixed signal, or RF). Minimum of 3 years of experience with Mentor Graphics (including advanced routing and stack up configuration).  Alternate routing software experience will be considered. Minimum of 3 years of working knowledge of IPC 2221, IPC 6012 & 13, IPC 7351, and GD&T for PCB design. Preferred Qualifications for Principal/Senior Principal Board Designer Expert working knowledge of the Mentor Xpedition software suite. Experience with high‑speed digital design (≥5 Gbps) or RF/microwave PCB design. Experience with High Density Interconnect (HDI) and/or Array designs. jobs.description_text: Director Product, B2B @ A Place for Mom You need to enable JavaScript to run this app. Director Product, B2B Location Remote-US Employment Type Full time Location Type Remote Department Product Compensation $180K – $215K • Offers Bonus • 30% of annual earnings Overview Application A Place for Mom is seeking a Director of B2B Product to shape the future of our Home Care business. As a senior leader within our growing Home Care product organization, you will define and drive our strategy to become an indispensable growth partner to home care agencies. You will be joining at a pivotal moment as we evolve from a simple referral network to a full agentic platform. Who you are: This Director of B2B Product will be at the helm of reimagining the agency experience at A Place for Mom. The ideal candidate is a strategic leader with a proven record of building and scaling high-impact customer products that drive measurable business results. You blend deep empathy for customers with a data- driven mindset, using insight and experimentation to translate customer needs into outcomes that matter. You have demonstrated success leading teams, inspiring innovation, and delivering tangible growth through bold product vision and flawless execution. You thrive in mission-driven environments and are excited to make a meaningful impact in senior home care by empowering families, improving lives, and redefining how consumers find trusted care solutions for their loved ones. This leader will report to the VP of Home Care Product, and partner with the team to formulate a long-term product strategy and vision that propels the product and business transformation of home care at A Place for Mom. What you will do: Product Vision & Strategy · Define and validate the agency strategy for the Home Care business, aligned to company growth and mission goals. · Identify opportunities to differentiate our customer tools, drive customer ROI, and achieve high customer retention and satisfaction · Champion innovation by staying ahead of consumer trends, technology, and data insights that shape product direction.
